first_impression.reaction: Googled 'prenup' because I've got property and super going into this marriage and I want to know what the rules actually are before I raise it. The first paragraph gives me the Act, the Part, a date stamp and the catch: it only binds if the technicalities are met and we each get our own lawyer. That's an answer, not a sales pitch. Then a Concierge link turns up in the third paragraph before the page has proved anything, so I went straight to the FAQ, then the requirements, the set-aside grounds and the overseas bit. Almost everything points to the court, Legal Aid or Moneysmart with links I can check. It also says plainly what it can't tell me, which I respect. What's missing for me is timing: how close to the wedding is too close to sign.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, it is only binding if it meets the technical requirements of the Act, and each of you must receive independent legal advice from an Australian lawyer before you sign.
journey.reaction: Dated, specific, and leads with the condition rather than the reassurance. Good start.

journey.quote: The celebration itself is where [Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=prenup&utm_content=primary) comes in.
journey.reaction: Sales link in the third paragraph of a legal explainer. I'm here about a contract, not a planner. Show me the facts first, then ask.

journey.quote: No. You cannot enter into a financial agreement without each first getting independent legal advice from an Australian lawyer.
journey.reaction: Straight 'No', sourced. That kills the DIY template idea before I waste money on one.

journey.quote: Until it is ended or set aside.
journey.reaction: Clear, and the follow-up explains how it's ended. No hedging.

journey.section: Who needs a prenup? Couples it often suits
journey.quote: No source says a couple needs one.
journey.reaction: That's the line that made me trust the page. Most sites would tell me everyone needs one and then point me to a lawyer they're paid by.

journey.section: Prenup requirements: what makes a binding financial agreement binding
journey.quote: Treat the financial advice as Moneysmart's recommendation; the court and legal aid pages make independent legal advice the requirement.
journey.reaction: Separates what's mandatory from what's recommended. That's exactly the distinction I'd check against the court site.

journey.quote: Openness about money is where an agreement earns its strength.
journey.reaction: Nice sentence, but it's the writer talking, not a source. The fraud ground underneath is the real point.

journey.section: Why some prenups are set aside
journey.quote: Victoria Legal Aid says financial agreements are legally binding unless it can be proved that: there was fraud; the agreement is not practical; it did not follow the formal requirements under the Family Law Act; there has been a major and unexpected change affecting a child; one person acted in an unfair way; one person did not follow the agreement; or property covered was taken by the government because of criminal activity.
journey.reaction: Two long run-on lists of grounds from two legal aid bodies, mostly overlapping. I read the first, skimmed the second. A short table would do it.

journey.section: Couples living or marrying across countries
journey.quote: For couples with a home, a business or family on two continents, that single point is often what starts the conversation with a lawyer.
journey.reaction: 'Often' according to whom? Every other claim here has a source and this one doesn't.

journey.section: What a prenup can and cannot cover
journey.quote: Anything beyond separation, from how you share accounts day to day to what happens to super, is a conversation for your own advisers.
journey.reaction: Earlier the page tells me super is one of the assets you can protect, and lists super-splitting among the set-aside grounds. Now super sits under 'beyond separation'. I think it means super outside of a split, but I had to reread it.

journey.section: What a prenup can and cannot cover
journey.quote: Legal Aid NSW says an agreement won't stop a court making property settlement orders in a case involving a bankruptcy trustee, and cannot be used to hide or protect property from bankruptcy.
journey.reaction: A limitation stated plainly and sourced. That's the kind of catch I want flagged.

journey.section: Step 1: Talk about it early, before invitations go out
journey.quote: How much lead time your agreement needs is a question for your lawyers, so raise it at the first meeting.
journey.reaction: Honest not to make up a number, but timing is the one practical thing I came for. It says 'early' three times and never says why signing late matters.

journey.section: Prenups for destination weddings and international couples
journey.quote: Legal Aid NSW says a financial agreement made overseas won't be automatically recognised in Australia, even if the agreement says otherwise.
journey.reaction: That's the real catch for anyone signing abroad, and it's sourced. Useful.

journey.section: Prenups for destination weddings and international couples
journey.quote: If you plan to sign in Australia and then marry overseas, ask your lawyer how the overseas ceremony affects your agreement.
journey.reaction: That's my exact scenario and the page punts it. Fair for general information, but it's the question I'd have liked at least framed.

journey.section: Prenups for destination weddings and international couples
journey.quote: The agreement stays with your lawyers.
journey.reaction: Good. They say what they don't do instead of pretending to be lawyers.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel and vendors with you, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: 'Fee agreed in writing before any work begins' is the only line that touches my real worry about planners. Still nothing on whether they take a cut from the vendors.

journey.quote: Once your lawyers have the agreement in hand, the rest of the planning can turn to the part your guests will remember.
journey.reaction: Brochure voice. Harmless, I skip it.

unanswered_questions: Why does signing close to the wedding matter, and is there any general guidance on how far ahead to sign? The page says 'early' but not why.
Can an agreement cover a business or family trust interest, or just personal property and super?
If we sign in Australia and marry overseas, does the overseas ceremony change anything about the agreement? The page only says ask your lawyer.
Does Wedded Wonderland take a commission or mark-up from the venues and vendors its Advisor books? (deferred business detail)
Is there a real destination wedding you've planned with the actual budget shown?

turn_offs_found.quote: The celebration itself is where [Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=prenup&utm_content=primary) comes in.
turn_offs_found.why: A CTA in the intro of a legal explainer, before any evidence. I came for a contract question, and a sales link up top makes me wonder whose interest the page serves.

turn_offs_found.quote: For couples with a home, a business or family on two continents, that single point is often what starts the conversation with a lawyer.
turn_offs_found.why: Unsourced generalisation on a page that otherwise cites everything. One 'often' with nothing behind it makes me check the rest harder.

turn_offs_found.quote: Openness about money is where an agreement earns its strength.
turn_offs_found.why: Emotional framing in place of the fact. The fraud ground says it better and is actually sourced.

would_share_with: My fiancee, the FAQ and the 'No source says a couple needs one' section, so the conversation starts from facts rather than me looking like I'm springing something on her
My accountant, the 'What a prenup can and cannot cover' section, before we both see lawyers

cta_reaction.why: The page earned credit: dated, sourced, honest that it's general information and that the agreement isn't theirs. 'Fee agreed in writing before any work begins' is the right line. But I came for a legal answer, not a planner, and whether they take a cut from vendors still isn't answered. They go in the comparison spreadsheet; I wouldn't enquire off this page alone.

top_3_changes: Give the timing section a sourced reason or general guidance on why signing early matters, instead of only 'How much lead time your agreement needs is a question for your lawyers, so raise it at the first meeting.'
Move the intro Concierge link below the key takeaways or into the destination section: 'The celebration itself is where Wedded Concierge comes in.'

Merge the two set-aside lists into one short comparison, fix the super wording in 'Anything beyond separation, from how you share accounts day to day to what happens to super...', and cut or source 'that single point is often what starts the conversation with a lawyer.'

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ first, looked for catches, flagged unsupported claims and early CTA
No invented brand facts; commission and real-budget questions placed in unanswered_questions as deferred
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored
General information only, no costs and no lawyer names by design, deferred business details and transfers, and brand sourcing silence not penalised

open_questions.question: Does the source pack hold any official guidance on why signing close to the wedding is a risk (for example pressure or unfair conduct), which could be cited in Step 1 without giving legal advice?

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for 'prenup' as an engaged groom with assets, comparing three planners, so relevance is 4 and enquiry likelihood is 2.
Missing costs and lawyer names are deliberate and not penalised.
The 5-minute budget covered the intro, FAQ, requirements, set-aside, can/cannot cover, steps and destination sections, with a skim of the second set-aside list.
